recG4mC1e79KaK37p.Bio: Jason Quitt is a Canadian author and researcher of ancient mysticism, sacred geometry and archaeo-astronomy, and the founder of The Crystal Sun. A graduate of the Institute of Energy Wellness who has studied energy modalities, shamanism and Qi Gong since 2002, he has taught and lectured on mysticism, meditation and out of body experience since 2010. His books include Egyptian Postures of Power, The Yosef Codes, Astral Genesis, Gates of the Anunnaki and Astral Experiences. His latest, The Shining Island: Precession, Axis Mundi, & Plato's Celestial Allegory, reads Plato's Atlantis not as a sunken empire but as a celestial allegory encoding the fall of the pole star and the precession of the Great Year.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title":"No Pole Star Over Atlantis","body":"Quitt says the thesis began while he was researching precession for his earlier books Gates of the Anunnaki and Astro Genesis. Winding the sky back to 9,600 BC, the date Plato's Egyptian priest gives Solon, he found no bright star sitting at the celestial pole. The pole instead fell between the legs of the constellation Hercules, which he reads as the two pillars of the cosmic man. Since Plato places Atlantis just beyond the pillars of Hercules, Quitt contends the date and the location are one astronomical statement rather than two unrelated details."},{"title":"Seven Sages and the Ark","body":"Quitt notes that Solon is counted among the seven sages of Greece, which he identifies with the seven stars of the Big Dipper, the pointers to the northern sky. Garton links them to the seven rishis, the Mesopotamian lawgivers, and the seven family members aboard Noah's ark. Between Hercules and Thuban in Draco, they argue, roughly 6,000 years passed with no pole star to steer by, a voyage through dark waters. Quitt adds that Thuban echoes the Hebrew word for ark, and that the Hebrew calendar's start date falls near Thuban's arrival at the pole."},{"title":"The World Soul's Concentric Rings","body":"Quitt argues that the Timaeus and the Critias tell one story twice. In the Timaeus the demiurge shapes the universe as a sphere, smooth on the outside, spun in place, its inner motion divided in six places to make seven unequal circles. In the Critias, Poseidon rings his island with alternating bands of water and land, cut as if turned on a lathe. Lay the two descriptions side by side, Quitt says, and the plan is the same. Garton calls it a quiet demonstration of as above so below, with Atlantis mirroring the turning heavens."},{"title":"The Red Island of the West","body":"Quitt sets Plato's sacred mound beside Egyptian cosmology, where Atum rises from the dark waters of Nun and fathers the twins Shu and Tefnut, and Shu is condemned to hold Nut apart from Geb. Poseidon plays the role of Nun, Cleito's hill is the first mound, and the firstborn son Atlas takes Shu's role as the axis holding up the sky. Hercules then sails west in the golden cup of Helios to the red island, which Quitt reads as the sun sinking into the sea. Garton adds that orichalcum may pun on oros, Greek for mountain."},{"title":"Hidden Keys and Polarized Societies","body":"Both men argue that Plato wrote in code because Socrates was executed for speaking plainly, so dangerous truths were folded into likely stories and the keys were handed out inside the academy. Garton contends that modern academics read the dialogues at face value and miss the indirect speech most of the world still uses. He reads the war between Atlantis and the proto Athenians as traditional society against progressive society, ending in mutual destruction, and notes that the word polarization itself points back to the pole. Quitt closes on aligning with the cosmic order instead of fighting the chaos."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Discover the real Atlantis in this deep dive into Plato's Timaeus and Critias. Jason Quitt unveils how the fall of the Pole Star in 9,600 BCE matches the "destruction" of the lost city.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: For thousands of years people have searched for the lost city of Atlantis, scouring the ocean floor and the far corners of the earth for a sunken continent, but what if Atlantis was never a place at all? In this episode, returning guest Jason Quitt joins Chance to unveil the central thesis of his brand new book, The Shining Island, in the very first long-form conversation recorded about it. Together they walk through Plato's two Atlantis dialogues, the Timaeus and the Critias, and make the case that the entire story is a celestial allegory, a creation myth written in the stars. The destruction of Atlantis, dated by Plato to 9,600 BCE, lines up with a moment when there was no pole star to guide humanity. This is a deep, dense, and genuinely mind-expanding conversation about the oldest story ever told, the story of the stars.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Vega and the Shining Island", "body": "Jason turns the clock back to roughly 12,000 BCE, the opening of the age when Atlantis would have stood at its height, and finds Vega in Lyra sitting on the celestial pole. Vega is about six times brighter than Polaris, the strongest north star of the entire 25,920 year precession, and if you plot the stars of Lyra wheeling around it you get concentric rings that match Plato's description of an island turned on a lathe. That picture, a brilliant center ringed by perfect circles of light and dark, is the shining island itself."}, {"title": "The Fall of the Pole Star", "body": "The destruction is not moral punishment but drift. Vega slips off the pole, the heavens lose their center, and around 7400 BCE Tau Herculis, a faint star in the leg of Hercules, briefly takes the position, which Jason reads as Hercules spinning aimlessly or falling into a hole in the sky. Then come roughly six thousand years with no usable pole star at all, the dark waters of the deluge. Atlantis sinking and the Athenians being swallowed by the earth are two halves of one celestial event, a bright order dissolving into unnavigable night."}, {"title": "Precession Read as World History", "body": "Jason walks the whole northern circuit as a chronology. Vega gives way to Hercules, then six thousand empty years run from the age of Cancer to Gemini, then Thuban in Draco arrives in the age of Taurus and civilization restarts with pyramids, written language, and the Sumerian and Akkadian creation stories, right where the Hebrew calendar begins counting. After Thuban comes Kochab and finally Polaris, the pole of Plato's own era and of ours. Vega and Polaris sit opposite each other on that wheel, twin luminaries splitting the great year into two halves of about twelve thousand years."}, {"title": "Egypt, Cygnus, and the Alpha and Omega", "body": "The pair push the story back behind Greece. The Eye of Ra, sent into the waters of Nun and returning to find another eye in its place, then raised to the cobra on Ra's brow, is precession told as myth, and Draco with Thuban is that serpent coiled at the temple of the sky. Further back still, around 16,000 BCE, Deneb in Cygnus held the pole through an era of mass flooding and dying megafauna. Chance notices that Cygnus reads as the scales of the age of Libra, with Delphinus, also called Job's Coffin, as the heart weighed against the feather of Ma'at."}, {"title": "Your Own Axis Mundi", "body": "The final stretch turns the cosmology inward. Osiris' spine is the Djed pillar, the four sons of Horus are the arms and legs of the cosmic man, and Christ as the body of the universe is the same figure in another dress. Chance argues the whole allegory exists to show that you are a fractal of that cosmos, and that the real initiation is becoming conscious of your own spine as an axis mundi. Jason closes with Timaeus assigning every soul to a star and the Pyramid Texts promising the imperishable northern stars to whoever lived well."}]

fields.Plus Quotes JSON: [{"text": "The entire heavens would rotate around Vega in perfect harmony and order, and it would look like an island, a shining island in the sky with perfect loops and water around it.", "author": "Jason Quitt", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/71bee0cb-99ee-4785-ba9d-5d867e75cbbe/JASON-QUITT.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "How do you navigate the world as a naval empire? You need a solid pole star.", "author": "Jason Quitt", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/71bee0cb-99ee-4785-ba9d-5d867e75cbbe/JASON-QUITT.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The monomyth really is the destruction and regeneration of the world and the world age doctrine.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "There is some kind of divine order that peeks through the blinders of history whenever you look at it in these big mythological frameworks, astrotheological frameworks.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "When you put it all together, it's too much of a coincidence that all these stories tell the same story, and all these symbols and myths tell the same thing over these thousands of years.", "author": "Jason Quitt", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/71bee0cb-99ee-4785-ba9d-5d867e75cbbe/JASON-QUITT.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "That's my favorite way to describe astrology is that the sky is the visible mind of God.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "You are made in the image of God. You are literally made in the image of the cosmos itself.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "When you die, you leave your body, you travel the stars, you go northward.", "author": "Jason Quitt", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/71bee0cb-99ee-4785-ba9d-5d867e75cbbe/JASON-QUITT.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "Whatever happens across that threshold, you are still you on the other side.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "What Plato is saying is you need to be aligned with the cosmic order and the cosmic harmony of this nature. And it doesn't mean closing your eyes to injustices in the world.", "author": "Jason Quitt", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/71bee0cb-99ee-4785-ba9d-5d867e75cbbe/JASON-QUITT.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}]
